subject.title: [Feature]: Support custom HTTP headers on CLI WebSocket connections

question: Should OpenClaw add a Gateway WebSocket custom-header contract, and if so which secret-bearing sources should be allowed: CLI flag only, env only, config `SecretInput`, or some combination with defined precedence?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing where credential-bearing reverse-proxy headers may live is a security and product contract decision rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Approve secret-safe core contract
options.body: Define header support centrally in the Gateway client/call path with explicit precedence, SecretInput/env handling, redaction, docs, and tests before exposing user-facing flags.

options.title: Limit to explicit CLI-only headers
options.body: Add a repeatable CLI flag only, avoiding durable config/env storage until maintainers approve a broader credential persistence model.

options.title: Reject core header surface for now
options.body: Keep SSH/Tailscale/local proxy workarounds as the supported path and document that authenticating reverse-proxy headers are not a core Gateway CLI feature yet.

recommendation.title: Approve secret-safe core contract
recommendation.body: Define header support centrally in the Gateway client/call path with explicit precedence, SecretInput/env handling, redaction, docs, and tests before exposing user-facing flags.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans the extracted Gateway client package, CLI call boundary, and Gateway credential precedence areas where this owner has the strongest recent history.
